clue.text: Idiot claiming trophy is limiting opening in computer science

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the idiot word wraps round the prize
a limit sits on both sides of what it bounds, so the short word goes around the opening letter
the opening of a word is its first letter, which is the only letter taken from the next word

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
taken as written, held inside the idiot
taken as written
first letter of computer, held inside the word is

explanation.surface: A fool grabs a prize while hogging the first place in a computer science course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'computer science' reads as one subject, but only 'science' is the definition. AS(TROPHY)S then I(C)S give ASTROPHYSICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrophysics is a branch of science, the physics of stars and other celestial bodies; the definition is a broader category.

clue.text: Describing bishop's area, I'd upset Saint in the main

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way
one thing set in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: the contraction without its apostrophe, turned round
S is the abbreviation for saint
the main is a literary term for the open sea

explanation.surface: Someone admits to being troubled by a saint at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic name for the sea, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Diocesan is the adjective for a diocese, the district under a bishop's authority.

clue.text: Eastern European's singular toilet

blocks.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
lav is short for lavatory

explanation.surface: An Eastern European owns a single, solitary toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive but stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slav is a member of a group of peoples of eastern and central Europe, such as Poles, Czechs or Russians.

clue.text: Surprised comment in school showing damage by fire

blocks.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
cor is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.walkthrough: Cor! is a British slang exclamation, much like 'Wow!'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is to burn the surface of something, a verb for harming it with heat or flame.

clue.text: Zero room in entire trans-dimensional passage

indicators.note: the zero and room are set inside the word for entire

blocks.note: entire means whole
zero looks like the letter O
RM is the abbreviation for room

explanation.surface: No space left anywhere in this passage through other dimensions.
explanation.definitionFit: A wormhole is a hypothetical tunnel through spacetime linking distant points, a staple of science fiction.

clue.text: Inclines to overlook a camera feature

blocks.note: leans means inclines, as a verb
the letter to be removed

explanation.walkthrough: LEANS without its A gives LENS.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens is the curved glass part of a camera that focuses light, so it is an example of a camera component.

clue.text: Small tablet in shed

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a pill is a tablet of medicine

explanation.surface: A little pill kept in a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like the garden building but is the verb meaning to let fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To spill is to let liquid or contents fall out, as one sheds something; both are verbs of losing contents.

clue.text: Shot possibly to fail in tournament

indicators.note: the failing word is placed inside the word for a tournament

blocks.note: a cup is a knockout competition
to lose is to fail

explanation.surface: A shot that may cost you the tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests sport, but here it is a camera shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a photographic or film shot taken from very near the subject; 'possibly' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Hitchcock film initially lacking obvious point for student of mental behaviour

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letters of the following words count

blocks.note: Psycho is Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 thriller
first letters of these two words
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A Hitchcock film that at first seems pointless gets studied by someone analysing minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' looks like a deletion signal, but it supplies its own first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychologist is a scientist who studies the mind and how people behave.

clue.text: Restore play area no longer in operation

blocks.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a British term for a public playing field
something over has finished

explanation.surface: Bring a closed playground back into use.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover something is to get it back or return it to a former state, so it works as a synonym.

clue.text: Mouldy? Has to end in decay

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, which is all that is taken

blocks.note: must means has to
last letter of decay

explanation.surface: Something mouldy is bound to rot in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Musty describes a stale, damp smell typical of mould, so the two adjectives are close synonyms.

clue.text: Nut? It is a chop that's cooked

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.definitionFit: A pistachio is a green-kernelled nut, so it is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Clear father turned up with mother, say

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
a mother is one example of a parent

explanation.surface: It's obvious Dad arrived with Mum.
explanation.walkthrough: PA reversed gives AP, then PARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means plainly visible or evident, a synonym of clear in the sense of obvious.

clue.text: Remains in the role of husband

blocks.note: as means in the capacity of
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' reads as a verb but is the noun: what is left after burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the powdery residue left after something burns, including cremated human remains.

clue.text: A variety of tripe provided as precursor to meal

blocks.note: taken as written
the five letters rearranged
if means provided that

the writer is the setter, who would say me

clue.text: King or Queen taking dinner, say, a bit at a time

dinner is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: Royalty eat their dinner slowly, in small bites.

clue.text: Circulating internet topic includes half of blue symbol

indicators.note: something circulating goes round, so the letters come back the other way
half of a word means only part of its letters are kept
to include is to hold within, so the colour fragment goes inside

blocks.note: a meme is an idea or image spreading online
the first half of the colour word

explanation.surface: A trending online subject contains half of a blue symbol.

explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a design or object representing an idea or group, so it is a synonym of symbol.

clue.text: Deduce liner, heading away, is carrying female

blocks.note: taken as written, then losing its first letter

explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence, a synonym of deduce.

clue.text: Fine, long-established congregation

something long-established is old

clue.text: Acknowledging crowd's applause after receiving 50 deliveries?

blocks.note: performers bow to acknowledge applause

explanation.surface: A cricketer bows to the crowd after a half-century in an over or two.

explanation.definitionFit: Bowling is the act of sending balls down to the batsman in cricket, each ball being a delivery.

clue.text: Gentle breeze, westerly at first, towards rear of vessel

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: first letter of westerly
aft is the nautical word for towards the stern

explanation.definitionFit: A waft is a slight current of air carrying a scent or sound, close to a gentle breeze.

clue.text: Error about the French church? Saying nothing

clue.text: Friday and every Saturday initially revealing side?

first letters of these two words
